title: U.S. House · California's 38th District
area: Southeast Los Angeles County and San Gabriel Valley, including El Monte, Baldwin Park, West Covina, and Whittier.

context.text: This is an open seat with no incumbent in the race, following California's 2025 congressional redistricting (Proposition 50). California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary; in the June 2, 2026 primary, Hilda Solis (D) placed first with 47.6% and Pedro Casas (R) placed second, advancing to the November general election.

candidates.name: Hilda Solis
candidates.currentRole: Los Angeles County Supervisor, District 1 (2014–2026); did not seek re-election to that seat in 2026

positions.summary: As an L.A. County supervisor, says she has led 14 motions in response to federal immigration raids, including legal action against unlawful arrests and seizures.
positions.quote: since the raids began, I’ve led 14 motions to protect Los Angeles County residents.

record.text: Authored SB 115 (1999), California's first environmental justice law, requiring the state EPA to adopt environmental justice standards; the Senate passed it 23-14 on 1999-05-24 and Governor Gray Davis signed it.

Authored SB 218 (1999), requiring courts to make domestic-violence protective-order forms available in languages other than English; the Senate passed it 26-5 on 1999-05-25 and it was signed into law.
Voted yes on AB 633 (garment-industry wage-theft protections, including joint liability for manufacturers and retailers), which passed the California Senate 24-13 on 1999-09-09.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists education standards, combating fentanyl trafficking, criminal-justice policy, border security, and addressing inflation and the cost of housing, food, and utilities as priorities, along with tax cuts and reduced business regulation.

positions.summary: Lists barring transgender women from competing against women in sports among his priorities.
positions.quote: Back to basics in sports by restricting biological men from competing against women.

positions.summary: Campaign priorities page lists supporting private school vouchers.
positions.quote: Support the implementation of private school vouchers.

statements.quote: Support law enforcement while opposing any defunding measures.
Address immigration reform, including securing the southern border.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No current campaign-issues page or public statements were found for Solis beyond her official biography, so no priorities/positions are cited for her. Her state legislative record (record items above, from official California Legislature roll calls) does not map squarely onto any of the guide's 15 fixed issue statements, so no vote-based positions were added; her extensive prior record as a member of Congress (2001–2009) and Secretary of Labor is not detailed here since it predates the 'record is what an officeholder did in office' scope available from the sources checked. A separately reported 1995-96 minimum-wage bill she championed (vetoed by Gov. Wilson, later enacted by voters as Proposition 210) could not be confirmed to an exact bill number and official roll call within the research budget, so it is not included. Pedro Casas: campaign priorities page (casasforcongress.com/priorities) is the basis for his entries. Biography gaps: Solis's education and early-career details come from Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, and her 2022 campaign page; no current campaign-site biography was loaded. Casas's biography is entirely self-reported on his campaign site, which also contains some outdated references to another district number.
